text: {"frames":["Luuk the ferrywoman has not spoken since the thaw, so when the mist-boat knocks twice against the jetty she only lifts a wheel of cheese from her lap. Its rind is cut into {a} equal slices, and the fog across the Tower canal will not lift until half of them are set aside. Luuk taps the rind with a wooden spoon and waits, her eyes on yours. How many slices make half of the cheese wheel?","A smell of warm waffle drifts down the stairwell of the mill, and Marijke the grey cat sits on the bottom step with her bell held silent. A round waffle lies on the windowsill, cut into {a} equal slices, and the mill door stays shut until the cat is given her fair share. She sweeps a paw across the slices, counting under her breath, and stops to look at you. How many slices make half of the waffle?","You shove the linen cupboard aside, and the humming behind it stops dead. On the shelf sits a round cheese with {a} equal wedges, and the humming belongs to a sly little goblin in a clog who wants half of them for his own hoard. He will sing his old song again only if you can say the number of wedges that make half. How many slices make half of the cheese wheel?","'Quiet, the canal under the floor is talking,' says Alfie, the boy who hears water, and he presses his ear to the boards. Beneath the trapdoor a wheel of cheese floats on the black water, cut into {a} equal slices, and the canal will only let the locks open if half of them are handed over. Alfie frowns and counts with his lips moving. How many slices make half of the cheese wheel?","Briony has been chasing the fog all night, and her jars are nearly full when the lids start to wobble. The only stopper that fits is a round honey cake, cut into {a} equal slices, sitting on the dresser where the mist can smell it. She needs exactly half of the slices to press the lids shut before the fog slips out of the Tower. Briony holds a jar up to the light and waits for you to answer. How many slices make half of the honey cake?"]}
